newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia palm oil ends with extended losses.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia palm oil ends with extended losses.

text.p: PALM OIL FUTURES PALM OIL PHYSICAL
Dec (3rd pos) 1,142 rgt/tonne Sept (south) 1,170
Open/Hi/low 1,158/1,158/1,141 Prev close 1,185
Prev settlement 1,165 * sellers prices

PALM OIL FUTURES - Prices ended lower, extending overnight falls on selling due to unsupportive September export data by SGS and expectation of poor data from Caleb on Oct 1. Lack of tenders news also drove prices to lower level, finding support at 1,141 and 1,142 for Dec futures.
PALM OIL PHYSICAL - Moved in line with futures, with interest seen among CPOs.
Third month December futures drifted in the range of 1,141 and 1,158 ringgit before closing at 1,142 ringgit ($452.09) a tonne, down 22 ringgit from Friday.
The contract next support level was 1,135 ringgit.

"The market was volatile and players sold more than they bought because of the underlying bearish sentiment," the trader said, referring to expectations of unsupportive September export data by cargo surveyor Caleb Brett on October 1.
On Monday, another cargo surveyor, SGS (M) Sdn Bhd, estimated September exports at 672,153 tonnes.
Lack of export tenders also eased the market, which had expected participation from India's STC and Pakistant.
There was talk that India's STC was in the market for November palm oil but traders were unable to confirm it. Sharp falls were seen in futures contract.
"Generally, the local palm market is still at a discount to soyoil, so I think the buyers will not switch over to soyoil despite its competitive pricing against vegetable oils," a dealer said.
He added that there were other factors for buyers to consider before switching to soyoil.
Trading was volatile with turnover rising to 2,364 lots from 1,112 lots on Friday.
The physical sector was trended in line with futures, and interest was confined to nearby CPOs.
Oct (south) crude palm oil was offered at 1,170 ringgit a tonne after trading from 1,175 and 1,170. Oct (central) saw bids at 1,160.
Oct (central) was offered at 1,140 with bids at 1,130 and Oct (north) at 1,130 and bids at 1,115.

Nov (south) crude palm oil was offered at 1,175 ringgit with bids at 1,165 after making sales at 1,180. Nov (central) saw offers at 1,160 and bids at 1,147.50 and Dec (south) at 1,175 with bids at 1,165.
In refined palm oil market, RBD palm oil was offered at $502.50 a tonne FOB Malaysia and Nov/Dec at $500.
Oct palm olein saw offers at $535, Nov/Dec at $525 and Jan/Feb/Mch at $530.
Oct RBD palm stearin was offered at $392.50, Nov at $400 and Oct/Nov/Dec palm fatty acid distillate saw sellers at $335. - Tan Lee Lee (603-230-8911) ($1=2.5060 ringgit).
